text.p: Seragen Inc said Tuesday that as part of a restructuring, it has amended its exiting licensing agreement with Ajinomoto Co Inc to defer and reduce substantially its financial obligations to the Japanese company.
The company said that Eli Lilly and Co has entered into a separate licensing arrangement with Ajinomoto and will assume most of Seragen's remaining obligation, subject to certain conditions.
Lilly and Seragen are collaborating on Interleukin-2 (IL-2) Fusion Protein therapy for cutaneous T-cell lymphoma.

In 1994, Seragen and Ajinomoto signed agreements that granted Seragen worldwide rights to certain IL-2 gene patents owned by the Japanese Foundation for Cancer Research and Ajinomoto for potential use in the development of Seragen's IL-2 Fusion Protein.

Seragen CEO Reed Prior said that if the company meets all the conditions stipulated by this series of agreements, it will realize a net cash savings in excess of $3 million over the next three years compared to its previous agreements with Ajinomoto and Lilly.

He added that Seragen's overall royalty rate payable to Ajinomoto upon sales of IL-2 Fusion Protein has been reduced significantly, aiding the company in efforts to raise more capital and find other partnerships to commercialize its technology.
